title: A Bridge for the Ledger
premise: In 1840s Singapore, Silas Blackwood, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Straits Trading Company, has survived five years by mastering silence. When a sealed letter arrives naming his family as conspirators in a smuggling plot they never joined, Silas discovers the company's ledger hides a darker trade: selling debtors' families into plantation labor across the straits. To save them, he must forge an entry that grants one last berth on the departing ship — but only one, and every choice damns someone he loves. In the end, Silas sacrifices his own freedom, taking the berth himself and leaving behind a hidden true ledger so the corruption will one day be remembered.
about_author: Casper Delacroix is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial shipping manifests in Southeast Asian port cities. His fiction excavates the silences between ledger lines, giving voice to those history recorded only as numbers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Silas Blackwood's POV. Opening in the flooded hold of a trading sloop, Silas recalls his father's drowning and the day the company claimed him as payment for debts. He demonstrates his hard-won skill of reading men's silences. Emotional beat: grief hardened into survival instinct.

chapters.title: Five Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A day in the counting house of the Straits Trading Company, where Silas copies entries and learns which questions are fatal. He observes clerk Ambrose Fenn hiding a sealed letter in the false bottom of a drawer. Emotional beat: wary curiosity stirring beneath obedience.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sent to deliver documents, Silas intercepts the letter meant for the company factor. Inside: names, dates, and his own family's name tied to a smuggling conspiracy he knows they never touched. Emotional beat: terror and the first taste of purpose.

chapters.title: Mother's Hands
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Ida Blackwood, Silas's mother, mending nets in the kampong. She remembers her husband's last voyage and the company man who counted her children like cargo. She senses Silas watching from the shore. Emotional beat: maternal dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas studies the company ledgers at night and finds the pattern: debts inflated, families transferred to the plantation ships. He realizes the 'smuggling plot' is fabricated to clear troublesome accounts. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the crime is arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ambrose Fenn's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ambrose Fenn's POV. The aging clerk, complicit for thirty years, recognizes Silas's curiosity and offers cautious mentorship — part protection, part confession. He warns that the last berth on the Meridian leaves in six weeks. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption through a boy.

chapters.title: The Factor's Smile
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Company factor Edmund Harrow interviews Silas, probing what he saw. Silas performs ignorance perfectly, but Harrow's parting words make clear the family will sail whether guilty or not. Emotional beat: the mask holding while everything beneath it burns.

chapters.title: What the Sister Saw
chapters.summary: POV of Mariel, Silas's younger sister, who works in the factor's house as a scullery maid. She overhears Harrow dictating the false testimony against the Blackwoods and steals a scrap of the draft. Emotional beat: fear transformed into quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Six Weeks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Family council by lamplight: mother, sister, uncle Tomas, cousin Dev. They count who can run, who can hide, who cannot move at all — grandmother Sefa, bedridden. The arithmetic of love begins. Emotional beat: hope and horror sharing one table.

chapters.title: The Berth Problem
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confirms the terrible truth: forged papers can secure exactly one passage on the Meridian. Each family member privately urges him to give it to another. Emotional beat: love expressed as refusal.

chapters.title: Uncle Tomas's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tomas Blackwood's POV. The pragmatic uncle secretly approaches Harrow offering to name real smugglers in exchange for two berths. He tells himself it is sacrifice; it is betrayal. Emotional beat: self-deception cracking under its own weight.

chapters.title: Night Copyist
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas begins forging the berth authorization, practicing Harrow's hand by candlelight. Fenn catches him — and instead of reporting him, teaches him the countersign seals. Emotional beat: trembling partnership across generations of guilt.

chapters.title: The Kampong Remembers
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida gathers the old divers who remember the night Silas's father died — and the truth that the company sank his boat over an unpaid advance. Memory becomes evidence. Emotional beat: communal grief becoming communal courage.

chapters.title: Harrow Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Harrow's POV. The factor, sensing leakage, accelerates the schedule: the Meridian will depart early, and the Blackwood transfer will be signed within days. He burns correspondence and promotes a watchful new clerk. Emotional beat: banal evil moving briskly.

chapters.title: Tomas Is Caught
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Harrow confronts Tomas mid-bargain and uses him: either Tomas betrays the family's plans or sails in chains. Silas learns of it from Mariel's stolen scrap. Emotional beat: fury at kin entangled with pity.

chapters.title: The False Bottom
chapters.summary: Fenn's POV. Fenn retrieves thirty years of secret duplicates from his drawer — the true ledger of every family sold. He gives it to Silas, saying memory outlives men. Emotional beat: an old man finally choosing a side.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The eve of departure. Silas must write one name on the berth authorization. Grandmother Sefa, lucid for the first time in months, tells him the sea gives back what is owed. Emotional beat: unbearable tenderness before decision.

chapters.title: The Meridian Departs
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At dawn, Silas writes his own name, hands the true ledger to Ida, and boards among the condemned. Mariel screams his name from the pier; Harrow watches, satisfied, believing the problem solved itself. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as surrender.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. On shore, Ida, Mariel, and Fenn begin copying the true ledger into petitions, letters, and whispers across every port town. Tomas, spared by Silas's gambit, turns crown witness. Emotional beat: mourning converted into momentum.

chapters.title: Across the Strait
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Aboard the plantation ship, Silas organizes the indentured with the only weapon he has left: their recorded names, which he memorized from the ledger. He teaches them to remember each other. Emotional beat: belonging forged in captivity.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Eighteen months later: the true ledger reaches a reform commission; Harrow's accounts are seized; Fenn testifies and dies quietly soon after, at peace. The first freed laborers return across the strait. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: A Bridge for the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mariel's POV. Years on, Mariel meets the returning ship — and Silas steps off it, freed when the transfers were voided. At their father's grave, she reads aloud every name from the true ledger, his last. Emotional beat: memory as homecoming; the bridge built at last.
